## Model and taskset

Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct has 7,615,616,512 parameters. Checkpoint files use BF16. The approved generation and audit runtime is cuda-fp32-eager-sm90-v1 (float32, eager attention, TF32 disabled); the signed training override uses BF16 forward/backward with persistent FP32 masters and AdamW moments. The signed manifest and role execution profiles specify the exact runtime. The active original MATH taskset contains 7,496 distinct usable problems: 6,746 mining tasks and 750 reserved held-out tasks. DeepMath and NuminaMath are not yet part of this contract. K=1 and L=1: one genuinely graded success and one genuinely graded failure for the same task on the approved checkpoint.


## How to start mining

Use a coding agent to read this guide and the repository guides, set up your
miner, watch discovery and diagnose failures. Keep watching this document and
GitHub main: fixes and upgrades will continue. Each epoch's signed source and
checkpoint take precedence over an older checkout. Never silently reuse an old
source, upload grant, deadline or model checkpoint.

Admission is open to every current subnet-120 identity with valid signed Affine
Ed25519 activation. There is no operator whitelist. Each epoch snapshots the
eligible identities; later activations enter a subsequent epoch. The signed
current manifest contains the actual eligible identity snapshot. Registration/activation is
separate from public dashboard access. Keep signing keys private.

Start with these concrete guides:
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MINER_QUICKSTART.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MATH_MINER_BOOTSTRAP.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/DISTRIBUTED_GPU_ROLES.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_CUTOVER.md

Use the exact runtime and hardware profile pinned in the signed manifest.
H200/SM90, CUDA FP32 eager, disabled TF32 and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
are the qualified profile. Core version pins are torch 2.14.0, transformers
5.14.1 and toploc 0.1.6. A package version alone does not qualify a different
GPU/runtime; follow the full setup/profile instructions. The manifest's numerical
policy is authoritative. The verifier computes a 152,064-wide distribution;
miners following the current compact contract upload only selected-token
logprobs, not that full distribution.

Read authority and current_url from https://affine.io/mining.json. Run the signed
source bootstrap using your private activated Ed25519 seed file:

CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 python -B -m subnet.source_bootstrap \
  --authority "$AFFINE_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY" \
  --current-url "$AFFINE_SIGNED_CURRENT_URL" \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/source-cache \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.key \
  --state /absolute/private/miner-state \
  --env-id affine_math --max-batches 3 --search-budget 8 --once

The search budget is a local per-task choice, not the signed attempt ceiling.
Start with eight attempts per task, then move on if no success/failure pair is
found. The current signed ceiling is sixteen. A local search budget cannot
extend it; use at most the ceiling in the current manifest. Spending the entire
budget on a consistently solved or failed task can consume the epoch without
completing a batch. Smaller local budgets preserve the original public draw
context, model, temperature, proof checks and three-batch quota.

The authority public key is
3301134b38401196d006a621ac4a772bb4b0e6afa15a7d34a0d1ae5f2c630bcd.
The bootstrap authenticates the signed pointer/manifest, approved source archive
and checkpoint file hashes. It admits the original task snapshot and executes
that signed code. Source approval authorizes execution; it is not a sandbox.
Your agent should monitor new epochs and launch each only once, inspect original
process handles after faults and never restart solely because observation timed
out. Do not share your wallet key, decrypted private upload capability or R2
credentials. Miners need no permanent bucket credentials.

## Current proof and learning contract

The active verifier is forced-inverse-cdf-prefill-support-v3. Public prescribed
draws bind the epoch, checkpoint, task, attempt, turn and token position. The
verifier independently recomputes logits, checks the selected tokens against
calibrated inverse-CDF intervals, checks TOPLOC and replays native outcomes.
Ambiguous intervals or support changes require exact cached-reference replay.
An unavailable reference is unknown, not fraud. TOPLOC alone and teacher-forced
log probabilities alone do not establish sampler consistency. Matching the
prescribed computation does not prove when or where it historically ran.

Upload selected-token log probabilities and TOPLOC under the explicit signed
selected-token-logprobs-v1 policy. Full-vocabulary probability arrays are NOT
required in the current contract. Token-only and prefill-only three-way research
policies are NOT active; do not omit required live proof fields.

A batch covers one approved mining task index on one checkpoint and must contain
one native-graded success and one native-graded failure. Grader faults/timeouts
are indeterminate, not negative samples. Held-out tasks cannot supply mining
batches. Complete token contexts, native outcomes, task/source/checkpoint
identities and sampler receipts remain required. Extra rollouts earn no extra
points. Same-epoch duplicate task indices across miners earn zero.

Training consumes committed-unaudited-training-v1 inputs after cheap identity,
format, task, checkpoint and commitment checks. It does NOT wait for inference
audits or reverify proofs. These inputs remain labeled unaudited. The trainer
performs task-normalized full-model BF16 updates with persistent FP32 masters
and AdamW moments, durably publishes the successor, and preserves optimizer
lineage. Only a genuinely published and qualified successor opens the next
mining epoch; follow signed discovery rather than an old checkpoint link.

## Continuous audits and proposed rewards

Seven admitted verifier workers claim jobs through the authenticated coordinator
API on Arbos.life. SQLite remains on that host; R2 stores immutable artifacts and
reports. The current operator audit scheduler groups at most four submissions
per job, selects up to 32 rows per tick, and allows 14 jobs in flight. Audit
selection and processing continue independently of training. An audit is a
sampled check, not a statement that all eligible contributions were verified.

The current continuous-probabilistic-audit-v2 score is unique eligible task
count multiplied by a miner validity estimate and confirmed-invalid penalties.
The current-cohort posterior bounds historical reputation. The operator policy
uses eight recent epochs, decay 0.8, Beta(1,1), an invalid multiplier of 0.1,
zero epoch score after two confirmed invalids, and a four-epoch blacklist after
three. Infrastructure and numerical unknowns do not count as valid or fraudulent.
Hourly raw points are summed and normalized once. Legacy bounded-random fields
in older manifests do not replace the continuous statistical contract. Use the
original signed opening, score policy and reports to inspect provenance.

The current pilot is NONPAYABLE. No new mechanism chain weights are submitted;
proposed scores are not a payment promise. Historical nonpayable epochs cannot
be made payable retroactively. Penalties concern rewards, never wallet funds.

## Durable storage and performance

R2 is authoritative for checkpoints, optimizer state, rollouts and reports.
Local storage is bounded disposable cache: retain current/in-flight owned state,
then retire obsolete owned files through coded lifecycle rules after terminal
jobs and durable ACKs. Active leases and unowned paths are protected. The cache-
stat successor has passed CPU qualification on all ten roles. Its guarded
finish-current recovery completed and the automatic ordinary controller is
running, with two ordinary completed warm-state epochs after recovery.
Long-term uninterrupted operation remains unproven. External miners must use
the current signed contract, never a research label or preparation alone.
The guarded coded recovery cleanup retired 51.99 GB of archived partial state
and 15.24 GB of an obsolete archived model; the current input checkpoint and
original failure evidence were preserved.

The larger matched 128-task checkpoint comparison completed: CP11 solved
77/128 (60.16%) and CP12 solved 86/128 (67.19%), with ten gains and one loss
on the same held-out tasks. This is a 7.03 percentage-point improvement on one
cohort, not sustained convergence. All eight original jobs completed, their
reports were archived and authenticated, and the research model replicas were
automatically retired after durable acknowledgement. Completed scientific
outputs were not regenerated during metadata recovery.

The separate matched 128-task CP13 evaluation completed: 84/128 (65.625%),
versus CP12 86/128, with seven gains and nine losses on the exact same tasks
and seeds. All four original 32-task jobs completed; their reports and archive
passed full readback, and the group-owned model was automatically retired.
CP14 subsequently completed the same 128 tasks and scored 78/128 (60.9375%),
with nine gains and fifteen losses against CP13. All four original jobs and
full durable acknowledgements completed; owned model retirement completed.
CP15 completed all four original jobs, full private R2 acknowledgements and
automatic replica retirement, and its dashboard row was published automatically.
It solved 85/128 with nineteen gains and twelve losses against CP14.
CP16 completed all four original jobs and full private R2 acknowledgements,
retired its owned replica automatically and published the sixth dashboard row.
It solved 87/128 with five gains and three losses against CP15.
Sustained convergence is not established. Failed-export evidence archival
after a genuine replacement ACK and durable retry are available as default-off
operator code; live adapter installation is pending and they are not part of
the running recovery source.

Verifier download-capacity admission and automatic per-checkpoint size metadata
are implemented and tested as operator code. They reserve missing
model and artifact bytes before backend execution, renew the original lease
on infrastructure deferral, and protect active checkpoint leases. The combined
worker rollout completed across seven roles; a subsequent source-bound validation
fix is installed on five restarted production workers. The remaining two roles
have finite research reservations. Deployment alone does not prove successful audits. The independently running metadata
observer follows genuinely published checkpoints and authenticated queued
historical jobs, and delivers signed byte inventories automatically. It does
not download models or provide proof-validity credit.

## Public interfaces and documentation

Read https://affine.io/mining.json for authority and current_url. Public
/llms.txt, /mining.json, /network-data.json and /reward-policy.json support normal
CLI GET/HEAD. Public dashboard access grants no private upload credentials.
Dashboard eligible-batch counts are not verified-proof counts. Independent audit
results are available only where an actual authenticated record exists.
